newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan may ease mandatory LPG stockplies soon.
newsitem.headline: Japan may ease mandatory LPG stockplies soon.

text.p: Japan's Agency of Natural Resources and Energy is considering easing stockpile requirements for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) importers by mid-December amid high global prices, an agency official said on Tuesday.
"We are planning to become a little more flexible on the requirements," he told Reuters.
A Japanese law requires LPG importers to maintain stockpiles equivalent to 50 days of imports, which equals about two million tonnes.
However, LPG inventories have been dwindling and may fall below the required level early next year as importers are reluctant to buy spot cargoes despite growing winter demand, traders said.
They are not buying spot cargoes to avoid giving Saudi Arabia a reason to further raise prices, they said.
The Saudi contract price is loosely based on the company's own assessment of spot market trends as well as the results of three monthly spot tenders.
The agency official said one possible way to ease the requirement would be to apply the inventory rule to groups of importers rather than individual buyers.
That meant an individual importers' stocks could fall below the requirement as long as the total held by the group met the requirement, he said.
He did not specify how the groups would be formed.
State-run oil firm Saudi Aramco has raised LPG contract prices for December-lifting by $60 from the previous month to $310 per tonne, both for propane and butane.
December prices are the highest in 16 years, according to the Japan LP-Gas Association.
Term prices for most Middle Eastern and Asian LPG cargoes are linked to Aramco's contract prices.
